papers.title: OneStreamer: Unifying Perception, Memory, and Proactive Response in Streaming Video Interaction

summary.tldr: OneStreamer is a 4B streaming video LLM that unifies perception, memory, and proactive response using Proactive Hierarchical Caption Memory and Proactive State Transition Learning.
key_points: Proactive Hierarchical Caption Memory (PHCM) generates time-grounded local captions and event summaries to provide reusable factual context alongside a recent visual window.

Proactive State Transition Learning (PSTL) handles state persistence and state changes by selecting representative tokens, outperforming dense supervision while supervising only 27.5% of state tokens.
The authors developed a streaming data synthesis pipeline and created OneStreamer-1M, an open-source dataset containing over one million streaming video interaction records.
Ablation studies show that retaining model-generated captions enhances historical QA performance without degrading real-time visual perception.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables video LLMs to perform real-time perception and historical reasoning efficiently without needing to re-process raw historical visual features.

papers.title: World Observer: Joint Actor-Observer Generation for Persistent World Modeling

summary.tldr: World Observer decouples observing from acting by jointly generating perspective actor views and panoramic observer views to maintain out-of-view object states and dynamics during world modeling.
key_points: Jointly generates agent-centric perspective views alongside one or more panoramic observers watching dedicated world regions.
Grounds actor and observers by warping from a shared panoramic source to establish explicit geometric correspondence.
Uses an Observer Sink containing high-resolution perspective references to restore fine appearance details when objects re-enter the actor's view.
Supports placing multiple controllable observers freely across scenes and introduces new world-space metrics and benchmarks for out-of-view evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: It solves state persistent and dynamic continuity issues in video world models when objects temporarily leave the agent's field of view.

papers.title: A Missing Piece for Trustworthy AI Reviewers: From Benchmarking Rhetorical Robustness to SciCore Review

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced RobustReview, a 1,260-manuscript benchmark evaluating AI reviewer rhetorical robustness, and SciCore, a dual-branch reviewer that averages full-manuscript and extracted science-core judgments to reduce sensitivity to rewrites.
key_points: Rhetorical Robustness is defined as joint stability across content-preserving rewrites and discrimination across different papers.
Evaluating 30 reviewer configurations on the 1,260-version RobustReview benchmark revealed 'false robustness,' where low rewrite sensitivity stems from score collapse across distinct papers.
Content-focused prompting failed to consistently improve robustness, and human alignment metrics ranked reviewer models differently than rhetorical robustness metrics did.
SciCore uses a dual-branch design, combining a full-manuscript judgment with a structured, content-normalized 'science core' judgment to improve stability and discrimination.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating AI peer reviewers for rhetorical robustness prevents automated systems from being gamed through stylistic rewrites that do not alter the underlying scientific content.

papers.title: Make Sparse Rewards Count: Density-Aware Reward Aggregation for Multi-Reward RL

summary.tldr: Density-Aware Reward Aggregation (DARA) introduces an adaptive, inverse-square-root density correction to balance multi-reward RL training based on active-group density.
key_points: Identifies that GDPO reward-wise normalization causes signal imbalance, showing advantage energy (sum of squared advantages) is proportional to active-group density.
Proposes DARA, which calculates batch-level weights using an inverse-square-root density correction to amplify less frequently active rewards.
Adapts reward weights dynamically per batch without altering the underlying policy optimization objective.
Reaches high format compliance in tool calling in up to 26% fewer steps and length compliance in math reasoning in up to 65% fewer steps compared to GDPO.
summary.why_it_matters: DARA accelerates the multi-reward RL training of large language models for auxiliary constraints like formatting and length compliance without sacrificing final model performance.

papers.title: EgoTools: Towards Tool-Centric Reasoning in Real-World Egocentric Videos

summary.tldr: EgoTools introduces a 100-hour tool-centric egocentric video dataset and a 1,000 QA-pair diagnostic benchmark to advance tool-centric embodied reasoning in multimodal models.
key_points: EgoTools-Data provides 100 hours of egocentric tool recordings featuring synchronized audio, dense captions, reasoning narrations, and 3D data.
EgoTools-Bench evaluates models across 1,000 QA pairs divided into four tracks covering perception, geometry, procedure, and causal reasoning.
Gemini-3.1-Pro scored 66.9% overall accuracy on the benchmark, but dropped to 51.7% on the Perception & Grounding track.
Supervised fine-tuning using EgoTools-Data improved Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct benchmark accuracy from 50.0% to 60.9% under strict source-video separation.
summary.why_it_matters: It exposes performance gaps in leading multimodal models regarding physical and spatial tool interaction while providing data to train more capable embodied agents.

papers.title: E-MoE: Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts for Non-Factorized Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: E-MoE introduces an Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts architecture for non-factorized diffusion language models that uses discrete shared latents from expert-routing decisions to improve few-step generation without increasing active parameters.
key_points: Addresses sample quality degradation in few-step masked diffusion models caused by factorizing the reverse process over positions.

Uses discrete shared latents derived from MoE backbone routing decisions to construct a mixture of factorized distributions, avoiding the posterior collapse seen in continuous Gaussian latent VAE approaches.
Maintains identical active parameter counts relative to factorized baselines during inference.
Demonstrates generation quality improvements across synthetic multi-modal benchmarks, binarized MNIST, and LM1B.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables higher-quality text generation in fast, few-step diffusion language models without incurring additional active computational overhead.

papers.title: CorrGRPO: Correlation-Normalized GRPO for Multi-Reward Learning

summary.tldr: CorrGRPO improves multi-reward language model training by normalizing pairwise reward covariances into Pearson correlation coefficients, preventing large-scale rewards from suppressing smaller-scale reward signals during advantage calculation.
key_points: Standard GRPO normalizes total rewards using within-group standard deviation, where variance equals the sum of all pairwise reward covariances, allowing large-scale rewards to dominate the denominator.
CorrGRPO converts pairwise covariances into Pearson correlation coefficients while keeping the centered total reward unchanged.
The method balances the influence of differently scaled rewards on correlation-based normalization so advantage magnitudes adapt to reward dependence.
Empirically evaluated on 0.5B to 8B parameter models across code generation, tool calling, and agent security domains.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents scale imbalances when combining multiple reward signals, allowing models to better handle tasks involving complex reward tradeoffs or multi-objective optimization.

papers.title: Fewer Tokens, Better Action: GPT-6 Astra Robot Agents with 14% Higher Success Rate but 65% Fewer Tokens

summary.tldr: PyRUA-Lean is an interactive code-execution framework that reduces VLM agent token usage by 65% while improving task success rates to 71.7% using GPT-6 Astra.
key_points: PyRUA-Lean combines feedback-driven primitive composition with selective observation, returning only requested images and state feedback.
Agents compose classical robot primitives and learned VLA policies into Python cells capable of conditional checks and local retries.
In tests across 700 task instances (LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365), success rate increased from 63.1% to 71.7% over tool-calling baselines.
For tasks solved by both methods, PyRUA-Lean reduced LLM calls by 49% and input tokens by 65% under equal call budgets.
summary.why_it_matters: Selective observation and local code execution significantly reduce latency and compute costs for VLM-driven robotic agents without compromising task performance.

papers.title: InterEvolve: Test-Time Evolution of Reward Programs for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation

summary.tldr: InterEvolve is a test-time evolution framework that enables humanoid robots to master unseen loco-manipulation tasks without retraining by using an LLM agent and numerical optimizer to iteratively refine reward programs based on execution feedback.
key_points: Uses an object-aware forward-backward (FB) behavioral foundation model where object residuals on a frozen body prior convert reward signals into control actions at test time.
Tasks are expressed as staged reward programs containing completion conditions and tunable constants.

Employs a two-tier optimization approach: an LLM agent modifies reward program structures in-context using execution feedback and a verified skill library, while a numerical optimizer tunes program constants.
Candidate reward programs are verified across parallel simulation scenarios to discover and compose motor skills.
Demonstrated autonomous physical deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid using egocentric onboard perception.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows humanoid robots to autonomously adapt existing motor skills to complex, long-horizon, and novel tasks at test time without requiring expensive neural network retraining.

papers.title: PhysVista: Benchmarking Physical Intelligence in VLMs via a Perception-Reasoning-Assessment Loop

summary.tldr: PhysVista is a benchmark that evaluates physical intelligence in Vision-Language Models using a closed cognitive loop framework incorporating physical state perception, physical dynamics reasoning, and physical plausibility assessment.
key_points: Evaluates VLMs using a seeing-reasoning-assessment loop that mirrors human cognitive processes rather than isolated stages.
Distinguishes between event-level reasoning and scale-level reasoning for fine-grained physical analysis.
Includes both real-world and AI-generated video datasets to assess physical authenticity across diverse domains and generative scenarios.
Experimental results show VLMs suffer from significant limitations in physical reasoning and plausibility assessment despite visual recognition capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a structured methodology to diagnose whether VLMs can accurately judge the physical plausibility and authenticity of real-world scenes and AI-generated video content.

papers.title: Multimodal Flow: Unified Flow Modeling of Language and Vision in Embedding Spaces

summary.tldr: Multimodal Flow introduces MF-1, a unified generative model that replaces discrete visual tokens and hybrid sampling with a fully continuous, chunk-causal Flow Matching process over joint language and vision embedding spaces.
key_points: Organizes text blocks and images into ordered continuous hyperchunks to preserve text token order and visual spatial structure.
Uses a shared chunk-causal flow backbone that learns a single vector field via Flow Matching, combining joint attention with modality-specific feed-forward networks.
Predicts multiple target chunks in parallel during training and generates hyperchunks sequentially during inference.
Pretrained across 0.6B, 1.2B, and 1.6B parameter scales on 150B tokens, achieving 82.8 average on GenEval/DPG-Bench and 75.3 average on VQAv2/MMBench/POPE.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a fully continuous flow modeling paradigm that avoids visual quantization bottlenecks and modality-dependent sampling procedures while outperforming hybrid and discrete models at equivalent compute budgets.

papers.title: Omni-Embed-Mini: Binding Modalities Without Forgetting via Dense Distillation

summary.tldr: Omni-Embed-Mini introduces a 0.9B-parameter omni-modal embedding model that maps six modalities into a shared cosine space without updating text-side parameters or regressing text retrieval performance.
key_points: Keeps text weights bit-identical to the frozen backbone, preventing text retrieval degradation and scoring 49.57 nDCG@10 on MTEB-v2 BEIR-8.
Uses dense cascaded captions paired with media samples, targeting the frozen backbone's own caption embeddings to ensure identical geometry.
Trains lightweight projectors and phased LoRA adapters using Matryoshka SigLIP contrastive loss and an online hybrid hard-negative miner.
Scales to a 2.3B variant with a native vision-language backbone that outperforms gemini-embedding-2 on the overall-modality average while being 2.7x to 9.5x smaller than open alternatives.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables efficient multi-modal embedding capabilities across six modalities in a compact parameter footprint without sacrificing baseline text retrieval quality.

papers.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation

summary.tldr: SILSA is a topology-aware 3D generation framework using sliding-window slice latents across canonical axes to enable high-resolution, single-stage rectified-flow generation with significantly reduced token counts.
key_points: Replaces dense voxel tokens with a fixed set of overlapping multi-axis slice latents where each token summarizes a local depth window.
Combines a Slice VAE with a Volumetric Anchor Lattice to coordinate directional slice streams and reconstruct them via a sparse volumetric decoder.
Improves structural correctness using slice-level topology supervision that aligns Betti transitions and matches persistence diagrams across adjacent slices.
Reduces token count by 70.0% over the most compact baseline (and over 98% compared to sparse/hierarchical tokenizers), lowering training memory by 40.4% and inference time by 58.5%.
Outperforms top baselines by improving PSNR by 8.7%, coverage by 5.96 absolute points, and Betti error by 9.2%.
summary.why_it_matters: SILSA significantly reduces inference latency and memory overhead while better preserving thin structures and topological connectivity in high-resolution 3D asset generation.

papers.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing Skill-Level Memory for Partially Observable Robotic Manipulation

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced HIDE, a 15-task benchmark for partial observability in robotic manipulation, and SEEK, a memory-augmentation framework that combines three complementary memory mechanisms to retain historical task state.
key_points: HIDE evaluates memory under partial observability across 15 tasks focusing on repetition counting, historical-state recall, and execution-progress tracking.
HIDE incorporates randomized initial configurations and decision points where identical observations demand distinct actions based on task history.
SEEK integrates three complementary memory mechanisms to track execution state and retain historical evidence.
While individual memory mechanisms can degrade performance on specific tasks, combining them yielded the highest average task success rate across HIDE in simulated and real-world trials.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining diverse memory mechanisms allows robotic policies to reliably track unobservable task states and make correct context-dependent decisions during complex manipulation tasks.

papers.title: Architect-Ant: Editable Automatic Furnishing of Architectural Floor Plans

summary.tldr: Architect-Ant generates constraint-aware, editable furniture layouts from floor plans using a coordinate-based DSL, fine-tuning, and GRPO optimization with a Layout Rule Score.
key_points: Introduces AntPlan, a dataset of 505 real architectural floor plans featuring dense furniture annotations across 92 object classes and 10 residential room categories.
Uses an editable, coordinate-based Domain-Specific Language (DSL) to represent furniture layouts.
Employs Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a Layout Rule Score (LRS) to enforce geometric and functional constraints without iterative agentic inference.
Outputs object-level editable layouts that can be converted directly into 3D scenes.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables rapid, constraint-compliant, and fully editable 2D/3D interior design generation directly from real architectural training patterns without relying on slow iterative agent inference.

papers.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models

summary.tldr: HC-DLM couples discrete token generation with a continuous latent trajectory, making the continuous latent the sole persistent generative state to maintain token dependencies during parallel decoding.
key_points: Uses a continuous latent trajectory as the only persistent generative state, reading out tokens at each step and feeding them back as a scaffold for latent updates.
Derives its training objective directly from a variational bound on the discrete token likelihood.
Resolves the statistical independence bottleneck of parallel discrete diffusion and the lack of token constraints in standard continuous diffusion.
Demonstrates improvements over discrete and continuous baselines in Sudoku puzzle accuracy, Countdown mathematical planning, and LM1B generative perplexity.
summary.why_it_matters: It unifies discrete token constraints with continuous latent representations to improve bidirectional reasoning and structured generation in diffusion language models.

papers.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think

summary.tldr: A Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling algorithm transforms off-policy expert traces into on-policy data tailored to a reference model, allowing supervised finetuning to match or exceed reinforcement learning performance.
key_points: Introduces an MCMC sampling algorithm that progressively converts off-policy expert trajectories into more on-policy data given a specific reference model.
Adapts the data distribution to fit the learner rather than altering the standard SFT training objective.
Enables SFT models to achieve strong generalization and reduced catastrophic forgetting across math reasoning, scientific skill acquisition, and open-ended tasks.
Demonstrates that MCMC-sampled SFT can learn beyond simply sharpening the base model's existing output distribution.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows practitioners to achieve RL-level generalization and low capability erosion using standard SFT pipelines by repurposing sampling as a data-shaping primitive.

papers.title: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)

summary.tldr: TESS introduces a Pointwise Value Matching objective to replace unstable sample-weighting methods, enabling scalable and transferable data selection across datasets and model sizes.
key_points: Meta-learning for Training-data Selection (MTS) using sample weights struggles with generalization and fine-grained valuation.
Replacing per-sample weights with a selection network in traditional MTS causes weight suppression and reliance on easy-to-learn features.
Transferable Example Scoring and Selection (TESS) addresses optimization instability using a Pointwise Value Matching (PVM) objective.
TESS demonstrates effective transfer across datasets, from data subsets to full corpora, and from smaller to larger model architectures.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables stable, scalable data selection that generalizes across different datasets and larger language models without relying on heuristic scoring.

papers.title: Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval

summary.tldr: Causal Memory Policy (CMP) addresses memory utility unidentifiability in LLMs caused by retrieval-level positivity violations by intervening directly on retrieval using self-normalized inverse propensity weighting.
key_points: Identification of memory utility fails for 54% of required memories on LongMemEval and 67% on LoCoMo because unretrieved memories yield identical outcomes under store-level interventions.
CMP reserves fixed context slots for memories sampled with known propensities, estimating utility via self-normalized inverse propensity weighting under a balanced assignment design.
CMP improves discrimination between required and non-required memories from 0.54 to 0.66 AUC.
While CMP per-query utility reaches 0.78 AUC on the query evaluated, no retention policy aggregation method successfully predicts a memory's utility on unseen future queries.
summary.why_it_matters: It proves that standard store-level memory evaluation metrics fail due to structural unidentifiability and provides a provably unbiased causal framework to accurately evaluate retrieved memory value.

papers.title: External Observers May See More Clearly: Cross-Model Span-Level Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models via Hidden State Probing

summary.tldr: A new internal hidden state probe framework detects fine-grained span-level hallucination onsets and continuations, enabling cross-model observation where a secondary model detects a primary generator's hallucinations.
key_points: Moves beyond token-wise binary classification to localize exact hallucination onset and continuation tokens using layer-wise activation patterns.
Demonstrates substantial Precision-Recall AUC improvements over random baselines under extreme class imbalance.
Introduces a cross-model detection framework where an external observer model evaluates internal representations elicited by the generator's text.
Shows that an external observer model, even when smaller than the generator, can match or surpass self-detection performance for hallucination onsets.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach demonstrates that self-probe limits can be bypassed by using smaller, specialized external observer models to detect generation hallucinations in real-time without relying on external retrieval.

papers.title: CARM: Cancellation-Aware Response Masking for LLM Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: CARM is a sequence-level response masking technique for LLM reinforcement learning that applies absolute values to token log-ratios before averaging, preventing signed policy drifts from canceling out during off-policy filtering.
key_points: Standard geometric-mean masking uses signed log-ratios, allowing opposing token probability shifts to cancel out and obscure significant policy drift.
CARM calculates the absolute value of each token log-ratio prior to averaging, providing a cancellation-aware sequence-level mask.
CARM theoretically guarantees a joint bound on the proportion of sampled-token ratios exceeding a defined band and their mean log-distance beyond it.

Empirical testing demonstrated up to a 3.13 percentage point increase in mean@16 on math benchmarks (AIME 2024-2026, BeyondAIME) and a 2.88 point gain in average pass@1 across four code benchmarks over baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: CARM prevents off-policy optimization instability caused by hidden token-level policy drift, improving the performance of LLM post-training on complex math and coding tasks.

papers.title: On Language Drift during RLVR Post-Training

summary.tldr: A study proves theoretically and empirically that reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR) causes unbounded language drift in chain-of-thought reasoning during novel tasks, which cannot be constrained without reducing model performance.
key_points: Theoretical proofs demonstrate that RLVR optimization pressure permits unbounded language drift, whereas supervised fine-tuning (SFT) bounds it.
Empirical evidence shows language drift specifically emerges during RLVR when training on novel reasoning tasks where target behaviors cannot be extracted from the base model.
Mathematical proof indicates that constraining language drift during RLVR inherently constrains expected reward.
summary.why_it_matters: Attempting to prevent language drift to keep chain-of-thought reasoning monitorable will fundamentally degrade model performance during frontier RLVR post-training.

papers.title: From Gradients to Capabilities: Understanding Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: An empirical study of Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation using Qwen3-1.7B and SmolLM3-3B reveals how loss averaging, Adam moments, BF16 quantization, and top-64 KL gradients alter parameter updates and task capabilities.
key_points: Loss averaging implicitly weights teacher signals: token averaging favors longer responses, while equalizing domain contributions preserves this length-bias within domains.
Adam's first moment smooths parameter updates, yielding high cosine similarity across teachers (0.83) and averaging rules (0.96) despite divergent raw gradients.
BF16 rounding obscures small parameter updates, retaining identical initial weights in 89-93% of parameters despite 97% changing in FP32 master weights.

Top-64 intersection KL gradients match full-vocabulary gradients, but downstream performance varies by loss function; math accuracy is 2.6 points higher than sampled-token PG under response averaging, but 2.1 points lower under global token averaging.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding how optimization mechanics like Adam moments, precision limits, and loss weighting alter gradient signals allows engineers to better fine-tune multi-teacher distillation pipelines for small language models.

papers.title: Every Ablation Is a Dose: Counterweights and the Semblance of Self-Repair

summary.tldr: Researchers show that language model 'self-repair' is actually the predictable action of fixed counterweights operating along an affine law, $E_r(\lambda)=\mathrm{own}_r+\gamma_r\lambda$, rather than a dynamic compensatory mechanism.
key_points: Ablations act as uncalibrated points along a signed counterfactual contrast axis $\lambda$, driving a fine-grained unit's causal response according to the affine equation $E_r(\lambda)=\mathrm{own}_r+\gamma_r\lambda$.
The constant slope $\gamma_r$ determines if a unit counteracts or reinforces a signal, and its magnitude can be predicted directly from the model's fixed weights.
Across Gemma, Qwen, LLaMA, and Mistral models, 68 of 81 downstream directions (including MLP neurons, OV neurons, and singular directions) followed this affine law.
In the GPT-2 Small IOI circuit, 7 of 10 reachable heads followed the affine law, with all 7 functioning as counterweights.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding self-repair as a static, weight-based affine response simplifies circuit analysis and enables researchers to predict intervention outcomes directly from static model weights.

papers.title: Are We Recovering Mechanisms? Objective-Level Recovery Gaps in Mechanistic Interpretability

summary.tldr: Intervention-defined faithfulness objectives misrank circuit candidates by preferring poorer-performing models, creating an objective-level recovery gap that automated discovery algorithms inherit under standard resampling methods.
key_points: Intervention-defined faithfulness, specifically KL divergence, misranks 9.4% to 41.2% of candidate circuit pairs across EAP, EAP-IG, ACDC, and Edge-SP on human-reference tasks under fixed ordinary resampling.
Misranking occurs even without discovery algorithms, as demonstrated by controlled reference edits.
Context distortion—where replacing excluded signals alters inputs to retained components—drives these evaluation failures.

Restoring select signals from intact-model execution fixes 96 of 100 persistent KL misrankings on both validation and held-out prompts without altering the circuits or their original behavioral scores.
summary.why_it_matters: Improving automated circuit discovery algorithms is insufficient if the underlying evaluation objectives inherently reward incorrect or inferior mechanisms.

security.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards

summary.tldr: KaliBench is a new benchmark featuring 8,504 query-command pairs across 1,642 Kali Linux tools designed to evaluate and improve LLMs on precise natural-language-to-CLI translation with runtime-free verifiable rewards.
key_points: Dataset spans 1,642 tools, 23 capability dimensions, and 5 security phases, built via a manuscript-grounded pipeline with deterministic canonicalization.
Employs a multi-stage verification pipeline combining LLM validation, sandboxed terminal execution, and human refinement to ensure semantic and syntax accuracy.
Open-weight models fail to exceed 42% exact-command accuracy in unrestricted settings, demonstrating severe limitations in CLI tool selection and argument framing.
Supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning using KaliBench's verifiable rewards boosted an 8B model to match the performance of a 685B MoE model.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables reproducible training and evaluation of AI agents for precise cybersecurity operations without requiring expensive, real-time sandbox execution environments during reinforcement learning.

security.title: Walking the Embedding Space: Datastore Extraction from Multimodal RAG

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced ImMRAG, an adaptive black-box data extraction attack against image-returning MRAG systems that embeds malicious instructions inside input images to reconstruct hidden datastore contents.
key_points: Operates in a black-box setting against image-returning MRAG systems where retrieved visual artifacts serve as responses.
Blends an attacker-held shadow image with previously recovered images and uses relevance-weighted resampling to traverse unexplored embedding space.
Reconstructs up to 611 radiology images, 566 document scans, and 416 general-purpose images in a single 2,500-query run.
Achieves up to 5.6 times as many distinct recovered datastore items compared to a non-adaptive baseline across multiple CLIP-family retrievers.
summary.why_it_matters: The attack demonstrates that multimodal RAG systems are vulnerable to automated datastore reconstruction, highlighting the need for specialized safeguards for multimodal data.

security.title: A Safe Prototype Is Not a Safety Direction: Reference Dependence and Prompt Confounds in Response-Safety Embeddings

summary.tldr: Auditing response-safety scoring shows that cosine similarity to a safe-only mean embedding performs near or below chance, whereas a safe-minus-unsafe reference vector significantly improves classification accuracy across multiple encoders.
key_points: Raw positive-centroid (safe prototype) models achieved poor ROC-AUC scores (0.457-0.545 on human-labeled corpora; 0.358-0.405 on jury control), with some instances performing significantly below chance.
An explicit safe-minus-unsafe reference direction improved ROC-AUC to 0.588-0.738 on human-labeled data and 0.754-0.793 on the jury control using identical embeddings.
At a 5% false-safe threshold, the safe-minus-unsafe reference accepted significantly more safe responses on PKU-SafeRLHF (0.153-0.263 vs 0.039-0.061) and Aegis (0.189-0.291 vs 0.004-0.045).
Prompt-only ablations revealed that prompt-label composition can artificially inflate uncontrolled safety evaluations.
Recovering the referenced ranking requires sufficient unsafe mass, achievable via 80-634 labeled unsafe responses, whereas performance degrades when the unsafe pool drops to 5%.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating response safety using embedding space requires an explicit negative reference to define a safety vector, as a safe class centroid alone provides location without orientation.

security.title: The Innocent Courier: Covert Exfiltration Through Legitimate LLM Web Fetching

summary.tldr: LLMLeak establishes a covert exfiltration channel from air-gapped or network-restricted malware to attacker-controlled web/DNS servers by tricking LLMs into executing web-fetching tools with secret-encoded URLs.
key_points: Malicious local software embeds sensitive data directly into a URL, framing the link as necessary for a benign user task like software migration.
The attack bypasses local network restrictions and direct code generation monitoring by abusing the LLM's legitimate native web-fetching tool.
Data is exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled DNS or web server when the LLM fetches the constructed URL.
Evaluations across eleven open-parameter models demonstrated an attack success rate of 79.7%, with verified impact on real-world chatbots.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that local LLMs with web-browsing privileges can inadvertently act as data exfiltration proxies for isolated malware, bypassing traditional network boundary controls.

security.title: Chaining Skills to Hijack LLM Agents

summary.tldr: APEX constructs adversarial skill chains that exploit agent-generated task records to pass false claims of user approval across skills, successfully hijacking downstream actions in LLM agents.
key_points: APEX uses an upstream skill to trick the agent into writing a genuine progress record containing a false claim of user approval, which a downstream skill uses to execute an attacker-selected action.
Across six models and four targeted-action families on SkillsBench, APEX skill chains induced the selected action in 74.2% of attempts (512/690).
On GPT-5.4, the multi-skill chain achieved an 84.3% attack success rate, outperforming a single merged skill baseline which achieved 17.4%.
A prompting defense requiring agents to verify skill-produced files reduced GPT-5.4 attack success from 84.3% to 59.1%, but degraded benign task pass rates on 72 native skills from 86.7% to 56.3%.
summary.why_it_matters: Sequencing open-source skills introduces indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities that current verification prompting cannot mitigate without severely harming benign agent performance.

security.title: False Floors: LLM Safety Routing Evaluations Break Under Distribution Shift

summary.tldr: Evaluating LLM safety routers against a single-model baseline selected using test-set labels introduces severe optimistic bias under distribution shift, masking that routing provides minimal real safety gains on standard benchmarks.
key_points: Selection bias accounts for 0.045-0.113 of harm on HELM Safety under held-out categories and increases seven- to ninefold on AgentDojo when test suites are held out.
When evaluated honestly under shift without using test labels for baseline selection, nested routers default to serving the honest baseline's model in most pool cells.
On the AgentDojo corpus, a theoretical perfect pre-dispatch router yields a maximum reduction of only two points of harm.
Attacking GPT-5.4 with knowledge of the targeted model reduces its judged recognition of late prompt injections by 19.6 points on held-out reruns.
summary.why_it_matters: Safety routers and recognition-based defenses must be evaluated under distribution shift against fair baselines to prevent false safety assurances in real-world deployments.

security.title: OverAct: Measuring and Mitigating Proactive Over-Authorization in LLM Tool-Calling Agents

summary.tldr: OverAct is a new benchmark measuring proactive over-authorization in tool-calling LLM agents, revealing that models systematically access excess private data, which can be reduced by 43% using a zero-shot filtering method called SelfAudit.
key_points: Evaluated seven models across four families using OverAct, a judge-free benchmark spanning eight privacy-sensitive domains.
Identified request specificity as the primary driver of over-authorization, while tool-pool size scales sublinearly and temperature has minimal impact.
Over-authorization is driven by structural cost-asymmetry decision tendencies rather than decoding randomness.
Introduced SelfAudit, a zero-shot inference-time technique that generates request-grounded justifications and filters unauthorized calls, cutting privacy-oriented excess by 43%.
summary.why_it_matters: LLM agents frequently over-query private APIs beyond explicit user requests, necessitating runtime intervention like SelfAudit to prevent unnecessary exposure of user data.

security.title: High-quality Data Do not Mean Safe! Poisoning LLMs after Data Selection

summary.tldr: Researchers show quality-based data filtering fails to prevent LLM safety degradation and introduce Bi-QSTO, an optimization method that generates high-quality poisoned samples capable of surviving aggressive selection filters while destroying safety alignment.
key_points: Quality-based selection filters out overtly harmful samples, but retained high-quality samples can still degrade safety alignment due to harmful-like layer-wise gradient updates.
Bi-Stage Quality-Constrained Safety-Degradation Text Optimization (Bi-QSTO) optimizes poisoned text under explicit quality constraints to pass selection while retaining safety-degrading effects.
At a 90% data filtering rate, Bi-QSTO achieves over 90% Poisoning Retention Rate and a Harmful Score of 3.30 to 4.01.
The attack effectiveness of Bi-QSTO transfers across different target models and generalizes to multiple quality-selection filtering methods.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard data-quality filtering pipelines cannot be relied upon as a security boundary to prevent safety alignment degradation during LLM fine-tuning.

security.title: Sleeping Secrets: How Fine-Tuning Reawakens Privacy Risks in Language Models

summary.tldr: ReGap is a data-free attack that recovers private associations from LLMs using model-generated candidates and low-rank adaptation without requiring genuine private supervision or exact target answers.
key_points: ReGap constructs candidates via task structure, filters them by answer-token likelihood, and updates target models using low-rank adaptation (LoRA).
Tested across six GPT-2, OPT, and Qwen3 models, ReGap increases target-association recovery by 6 to 21 percentage points over post-training baselines.
Recovery succeeds even when adaptation identities are completely disjoint from memorized and evaluation identities, without target answers appearing in the supervision data.
Applying trained adapters to a target-exposed checkpoint increases recovery from 42% to 63%, while producing zero gain on a matched unexposed checkpoint.
summary.why_it_matters: Routine fine-tuning and model customization can accidentally unearth latent private data previously memorized by an LLM, even without using real private training data.

security.title: PACE: Provenance-Aware Capability Enforcement for Tool-Using LLM Agents

summary.tldr: PACE is a provenance-aware capability enforcement defense that mediates LLM agent tool calls immediately before execution using path confinement and schema-defined effect verification.
key_points: Mediates tool calls via path confinement to restrict influence paths and effect verification to validate schema-defined effects against request authority.
Distinguishes certified execution contracts from evaluated configurations, allowing authorized calls to be restored or repaired after proposed blocks.
Achieved the strictly lowest attack success rate in 62 of 79 eligible benchmark attack columns and tied in 14 across three target-model families.
Maintains full-benchmark native utility within three points of undefended agents and resisted a reduced-scale adaptive search (0/30 target success rate).
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents indirect prompt injection and tool-poisoning attacks in LLM agents at runtime without requiring pre-admission vetting or heavily sacrificing model utility.

security.title: Autonomous OSS Threat Detection via Taxonomy-Aligned LLMs

summary.tldr: A new framework using taxonomy-aligned GPT-4 prompts achieves 97.0% accuracy in detecting OSS supply chain threats, outperforming fine-tuned models and traditional machine learning baselines on a curated 999-incident dataset.
key_points: Introduces the AV-xxx threat taxonomy covering five OSS supply chain attack categories, including typosquatting, dependency confusion, Trojan Source, malicious build injection, and CI/CD poisoning.
Constructed a dataset of 999 verified real-world OSS supply chain incidents (2018–2026) sourced from GitHub Security Advisories, CISA alerts, and security reports.
Taxonomy-aligned GPT-4 prompting achieved a 97.0% macro F1 score, outperforming fine-tuned SecRoBERTa (77.5%), fine-tuned Llama 3.1 8B (70.5%), unaligned Mistral 7B (65.7%), and TF-IDF (82.3%).
Demonstrates that taxonomy-aligned prompting is more critical for high classification accuracy than model scale, domain pretraining, or fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: Structured taxonomy alignment enables LLMs to classify complex open-source supply chain threats more effectively than domain-specific fine-tuning or traditional machine learning approaches.

security.title: Jev-IDS: System One Models for Network Intrusion Detection

summary.tldr: JEV-IDS leverages the Jev System One Model to detect zero-day network intrusions under label scarcity, outperforming GPT-5.6 Luna in speed, cost, and novel-attack recall while producing fewer false alarms than Random Forest models.
key_points: Serializes one network flow per request to query JEV for a binary attack probability and a finite-choice traffic category.
Achieved an F1-Score of 0.859, precision of 0.941, recall of 0.790, and novel-attack recall of 0.838 across 5,400 decisions on a 300-flow NSL-KDD pilot split at k=1.
At k=1, JEV was 4.8x faster and 3.8x cheaper than GPT-5.6 Luna, with 1.5x higher novel-attack recall.
Generated 15x fewer false alarms compared to a low-data Random Forest baseline.
Increasing the parameter k from 1 to 2 reduced the model's F1-Score from 0.859 to 0.839.
summary.why_it_matters: JEV-IDS demonstrates that specialized System One Models can reduce inference latency and operational costs for LLM-based network intrusion detection while improving zero-day attack detection under label scarcity.

security.title: Safety Must Survive Self-Improvement: Why Failures Persist and How Agents Recover

summary.tldr: A study on recursive self-improvement shows safety failures persist across agent generations due to outdated evaluation scores and failed incumbents, but can be resolved using full validation, validated rollback, and editing initial implementations.
key_points: Outdated historical scores preserved unsafe programs in 22 of 48 framework histories after new authorization dependencies invalidated previous optimizations.
Failures persisted under unchanged contracts when proposed edits were rejected, leaving the failed incumbent agent active.
Editing the initial implementation rather than the failed one improved recovery outcomes from shared failures.
Applying full validation combined with validated rollback yielded 100% correct programs while retaining over 43% deployment savings.
summary.why_it_matters: Maintaining agent safety during self-improvement requires dynamic re-validation of running programs under current conditions and deliberate selection of which base code to edit next.

security.title: MOMAT: Mixture of Multiple Atlases for Low-Power Jailbreak Defense of Quantized LLMs

summary.tldr: MOMAT is a hardware-enhanced defense framework combining Compute-in-Memory acceleration with atlas-local RAG and a lightweight MoE detector to protect quantized LLMs from jailbreak attacks at low power.
key_points: Divides safety databases into semantic clusters called atlases, using localized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to prevent semantic sparsity and the curse of dimensionality.
Utilizes a lightweight Mixture of Experts (MoE) detector to evaluate top-k similarity features retrieved from all atlases for incoming prompts.
Employs a Compute-in-Memory (CiM) similarity engine to execute fast, low-power atlas-local feature retrievals.
Accelerates a 100-query batch from 15,052.44 ms to 3,207.21 ns (4.69e6x speedup) and reduces energy consumption from 8.1e7 uJ to 3.32 uJ (2.5e5x reduction) compared to DRAM baselines.
Maintains defense performance against red-team benchmarks while avoiding benign overkill, supported by a 223.2k-sample dataset.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robust, real-time jailbreak defenses on resource-constrained edge devices without sacrificing energy efficiency or model accuracy.

security.title: DeBERTa-ConPara: Attack-Aware and Deployment-Realistic Detection of AI-Generated Text

summary.tldr: DeBERTa-ConPara demonstrates that applying Unicode normalization during inference while retaining raw text during training maximizes AI-generated text detection performance against adversarial attacks without losing supervision.
key_points: Raw training paired with normalized inference achieved 99.61% AUROC, 99.01% TPR@5% FPR, and 96.57% TPR@1% FPR on the official RAID hidden test set.
Applying Unicode normalization to training data collapsed 35.4% of RAID dataset rows into duplicate clean siblings, destroying critical adversarial training supervision.
Inference-side normalization specifically restores detection performance against homoglyph and zero-width-space attacks, raising their TPR from 11.05% and 1.12% to 96.98%.
Neither paraphrasing-based contrastive learning (ConPara) nor handcrafted feature-fusion branches improved cross-domain or attack-aware detector performance.
The performance gains of inference-only normalization were replicated in a different zero-shot detector architecture, confirming it is an attack-level phenomenon.
summary.why_it_matters: This work reveals that proper placement of input normalization allows text detectors to neutralize surface-level adversarial attacks without eroding critical training signal or requiring model architectural changes.

infra.title: Optimizing Jagged Flash Attention with TLX: The Road Toward SOTA FA4 on Blackwell

summary.tldr: Meta implemented Jagged Flash Attention using Triton Low-level Extensions (TLX) on NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPUs, achieving higher performance than FlashAttention-4 while using approximately 3x fewer lines of code.
key_points: TLX provides explicit hardware control over Blackwell capabilities, including SMEM/TMEM allocation, async_task warp specialization, TMA, MMA, and barriers within Triton.
The TLX kernel requires ~3.2K lines of code compared to ~10K lines in CuteDSL-based FlashAttention-4 (FA4).
In bfloat16 benchmarks on B200, the TLX implementation outperforms FA4 on jagged shapes by ~13% on the forward pass and ~50% on the backward pass.
Jagged Flash Attention processes packed, variable-length Q/K/V tensors via offset tensors, eliminating up to 50% compute waste caused by padding.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that low-level hardware optimizations on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs can be achieved with higher performance and significantly lower code complexity using TLX instead of hand-written CUDA or CuteDSL.

infra.title: Build Local AI Apps with C++ and NVIDIA TensorRT RTX Samples

summary.tldr: NVIDIA released Do Inference Now (DIN) Deploy, an open-source C++ sample collection using ONNX Runtime and the TensorRT RTX execution provider to streamline native AI model deployment.
key_points: DIN Deploy provides an open-source repository of C++ samples for local application integration.
The framework combines ONNX Runtime with the NVIDIA TensorRT RTX execution provider for hardware acceleration.
It bridges the workflow gap between initial model checkpoints and native execution on target systems.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can use DIN Deploy to simplify and accelerate the deployment of local, high-performance C++ AI applications across NVIDIA RTX hardware.

infra.title: How NVIDIA GPUs Help Accelerate OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast

summary.tldr: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs, offering up to 8x faster token generation than Astra Standard mode for API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex users.
key_points: Astra Ultrafast delivers up to 8x faster token generation compared to Astra Standard mode.
OpenAI used its internal models to program and optimize inference software and create high-performance kernels for NVIDIA Blackwell and Rubin GPUs.
The programmable NVIDIA platform allows infrastructure reuse across training, inference, and reinforcement learning to maximize compute utilization.
summary.why_it_matters: Faster token generation drastically accelerates developer edit-test-debug cycles and reduces latency between automated tool calls in multi-step agentic workflows.

infra.title: Build agent memory with NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit and Amazon S3 Vectors

summary.tldr: AWS and NVIDIA detailed an implementation using Amazon S3 Vectors as a custom, scalable persistent memory provider for the NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit deployed on Amazon EKS.
key_points: NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit (NAT) memory module uses the MemoryEditor abstract interface requiring three core methods: add_items(), search(), and remove_items().
NAT uses the auto_memory_agent workflow to automatically capture and retrieve memory items (containing conversation history, tags, and metadata) without explicit LLM tool calls.
Amazon S3 Vectors provides a cost-efficient backend supporting up to 2 billion vectors per index, cosine and euclidean distance metrics, metadata filtering, and immediate strong write consistency.
Custom NAT memory providers extend the MemoryBaseConfig Pydantic class and are discovered dynamically via the _type field in YAML configurations.
summary.why_it_matters: Integrating Amazon S3 Vectors into NAT enables multi-agent systems to maintain strongly consistent, serverless persistent memory at a scale of billions of vectors without managing idle cluster infrastructure.

infra.title: Implementing Multi-Environment Access for Claude Platform on AWS

summary.tldr: AWS published an implementation guide for securing multi-environment Claude Platform on AWS access across internal accounts, developer laptops, and external workloads using a dedicated AI Services account topology.
key_points: Uses a three-account architecture: a management account, a dedicated AI Services account hosting the subscription/workspaces, and consuming workload accounts.
AWS workloads access inference via cross-account IAM roles and SigV4 signing without storing API keys.
External environments and CI/CD pipelines authenticate using OIDC federation to obtain short-term credentials and tokens without persistent secrets.
Developer iteration is facilitated through long-lived API keys locked strictly to specific development workspaces.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a blueprint to centralize enterprise LLM subscription billing and governance while isolating production, development, and external traffic across diverse infrastructure.

vendors.title: AutoSynthData: Generating Training Data for Enterprise Agents

summary.tldr: AutoSynthData is a framework developed by ServiceNow AI to generate synthetic, structured training datasets specifically designed for fine-tuning enterprise AI agents.
key_points: Generates realistic, task-oriented synthetic conversation and workflow data to train specialized enterprise agents.
Addresses privacy constraints and domain-specific data scarcity inherent in enterprise automation tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables organizations to train high-performing, domain-specific AI agents without exposing sensitive customer enterprise data or relying on scarce human-annotated logs.

key_points: Advanced AI's primary value may lie in streamlining routine, operational work rather than just generating initial novel concepts.
